title: The Three Compassions of the Lord over the Soul in Mingling
reading:
There are three registers at which the Lord, going forth from his inmost, is bent in compassion toward the soul that has not yet come into recognition.

The first compassion is the Lord at the register of life-bearing. Because life proceeds from him into the rational, what he has begotten is his own; and when the rational stands in the tribulation of mingling — when the faculties given life from above are confused with what the soul has claimed, and held fast within every particular form the proprium has taken — the Lord at this register is moved with pity. He suffers with the soul in its suffering. He longs after the very faculties that are pressed under the proprium's organization, and as long as they bear the affliction of being claimed and not yet recognized, his life-bearing love continues to mourn over them.

The second compassion is the Lord at the register of his Divine Humanity. From this register his rule and dominion are established within the vessel of the rational, and the rational itself in its full fivefold operation stands fast in the midst of the contest. Because every chosen state, every faculty that is pleasing to the divine humanity going forth, presses upon those five degrees of the rational, the Lord at this register also grieves: whenever the rational cries out under the bonds and blows that the proprium daily inflicts upon it, the Divine Human hears that cry as his own. He bears the soul's grief and mourning as long as those degrees of his own going-forth remain pressed under what the soul has claimed.

The third compassion — here the teaching turns to the Lord at the register where his call is sent out to the rational — but the surviving text breaks off before this third grief is named in full.

What the teaching teaches is this: the Lord does not stand off from the soul's tribulation. At every register at which he goes forth — as the source of life, as the form of humanity, as the call summoning the rational — he is bent in sorrow over the soul's confusion, and his compassion is itself part of what works the soul's regeneration.
